item.title: Weekly Newsletter #14 — February 26, 2026
item.description:
🔥 TONIGHT: FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

TONIGHT at 6pm, join our Housing Committee for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

We will be hosting it at Indy Hall and providing hoagies, beer, and seltzers.

RSVP HERE

🚏 PICK A LOCATION FOR THE NEW INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is working on plans for a permanent, publicly owned intercity bus station, and your voice is needed.

They're conducting a survey to evaluate three different locations--we recommend responding with 30th and Arch as your preferred choice. 

💳 SAVE ZERO FARE AND SEPTA KEY ADVANTAGE

The next city budget may cut the hugely successful Zero Fare program and SEPTA Key Advantage for City employees.

Our advocates fought hard for these two programs which together provide reduced-fare or fare-free SEPTA access for over 70,000 Philadelphians--don't let them get cut!

Sign Transit Forward Philadelphia's petition calling on the City to keep these vital programs.

And get involved by attending one of their events! 

  • February 28th (3:00pm-5:00pm) - Transit Rider Canvass - York Dauphin Station
  • March 2nd
    • (5:30pm-7:00pm) - Content Creation Training - 1500 Walnut Suite 1107
    • (7:00pm-8:00pm) - Advocacy Training - 1500 Walnut Suite 1107 + Virtual Option
  • March 3rd
    • (10:00am-12:00pm) - Zero Fare Advocacy Day - City Hall
    • (5:00pm-8:00pm) - Art Build - Spiral Q
  • March 6th (10:00am) - Rally and Press Conference

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🗳️ Run for Committee Person

Running for committee person is surprisingly easy and impactful! Our sister-org 5th Square PAC is encouraging you to run and is providing a tool kit to help you get elected. Sign up here to receive a toolkit of voter lists, how-to guides, and petition forms.

🚏 Intercity Bus Terminal Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is planning for a future intercity bus station and they're looking for feedback about three possible locations. We recommend selecting 30th and Arch as your preferred location. Take their survey here.

🚧 Safer West Market St

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads. There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024. We're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

EVENTS

Urbanist Fireside Chat with Angela Brooks
February 26, 6pm to 8pm | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join our Housing Committee for a “fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

DVRPC Planning and Funding Transportation Infrastructure Across the Region
Mar 4, 06:00 PM | Virtual via Zoom
Join DVRPC for a webinar that will inform and engage residents in major regional planning and transportation initiatives. It will provide an overview of long-range planning efforts for Update: Connections 2050, explain the Transportation Improvement Program (TIP), how projects are prioritized, and show how residents can provide feedback to help shape planning decisions.

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference
Thursday, March 12th, 9:00am to 4:00pm | Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St
This year's Vision Zero conference, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety", invites participants to explore how the physical, social, and economic city converge and what’s possible when community needs and lived experiences guide decisions

WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Inquirer.com / Pennsport apartment tower secures $150 million construction loan, plans to break ground next year
  • The Atlantic / High-End Construction Really Does Help Everyone
  • Mercatus Center / How to Streamline Housing Permitting in Pennsylvania

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • Inquirer.com / Chinatown Stitch, which would cap the Vine Street Expressway, is in limbo after Trump yanked funds. Can it be saved?
  • fitlerfocus.com / What Runs Beside the Trail? City and CSX Withhold Hazardous Rail Cargo Details
  • Philadelphia Magazine / How to Save Market East (For Real This Time)
  • Inquirer.com / Philly has lots of trails. For the first time, it is hiring a full-time crew to maintain them.

🚌 TRANSIT

  • Inquirer.com / Philly’s Greyhound station is one step closer to finding a permanent home
  • Greater Greater Washington / MARC should join SEPTA to buy new Silverliner VI trains

🚲 MOBILITY

  • makedrivingsuckless.substack.com / All Center City deliveries should be made by cargo bike

JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Bicycle Transit Systems / Field Technician - Indego Bike Share

PA Department of Community & Economic Development / Deputy Secretary for Housing

AARP / Community Challenge Grant

America Walks / Walking College

City of Philadelphia

  • Manager, Business Development
  • Flood Resilience Specialist
  • Deputy Managing Director, Division
  • Internship (OTIS)

Leadership Philadelphia / CEO

Committee of Seventy / Documenters Program Manager

Vital City / Policy Director

Transit for All PA / Digital Organizer - Data Lead

Do you like this newsletter and our advocacy work? 
We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement (and get cool perks)
Join us as a member TODAY! 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents.

Donations are not tax deductible.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #13 — February 19, 2026
item.description:
🔥 NEXT WEEK: FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

Next week on Thursday, February 26th, join our Housing Committee for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

We will be hosting it at Indy Hall and providing hoagies, beer, and seltzers.

RSVP HERE

🚸 SCHOOL ZONE SPEED CAMERAS

Earlier this week, the PPA officially turned on speed cameras in five high-crash school zones throughout the city. Following a 60-day warning period, drivers who speed during school hours will begin to receive tickets.

Thank you to CM Thomas for sponsoring legislation to enable this pilot program! We look forward to seeing these five schools become safer, and we hope to see the program expanded to other schools.

🚏 INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL OPEN HOUSE AND SURVEY

Next Wednesday, the Philadelphia City Planning Commission is hosting a public open house on plans for a permanent, publicly owned intercity bus station, and your voice is needed.

Wednesday, February 25, 2026  from 6:00–8:00 PM
Independence Visitor Center, 599 Market Street

This is our chance to push for a new intercity bus station that treats riders with the dignity they deserve, strengthens our city's transit connections around the region and country, and supports a more equitable Philadelphia for decades to come. Stay in the loop by signing up with our friends at Transit Forward Philadelphia 

CPC is also conducting a survey to help them evaluate three different locations they are currently considering.

🗳️ RUN FOR COMMITTEE PERSON

Our sister-org 5th Square PAC is encouraging you to run for the city's most local political office this spring: Committee Person.

These roles are the "foot soldiers" of Philadelphia’s political parties, and by serving in your voting division, you can help reform the political machine, make ward committees more democratic, and ensure we elect representatives who support urbanist positions.

Starting this week, you can get on the ballot by collecting a few dozen signatures from your neighbors; whether you are ready to run or just want more information, SIGN UP HERE to receive a toolkit of voter lists, how-to guides, and petition forms.

🎰 HORSE RACING OR TRANSIT FUNDING?

At a time when Harrisburg is unable to find money in the budget to fund PA's transit agencies, we still somehow have enough money to give the horse racing industry $200 million every year. And now, House Bill 2071 is seeking to increase that amount.

We oppose sending gambling revenue to subsidize horse racing while public transit systems are being forced to cut services and increase fares around the state.

An anti-horse racing coalition organized a petition calling on the PA legislature to end taxpayer support for horse racing. Sign it here.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚏 Intercity Bus Terminal Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is planning for a future intercity bus station and they're looking for feedback about three possible locations. Take their survey here.

🚧 Safer West Market St

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads. There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024. We're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

EVENTS

Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Conference
Fri, Feb 20, at 8:30 AM | The Study at University City, 20 S 33rd St
The Future of Cities Conference is a student-led, faculty-advised conference that aims to bring together urban innovators and experts from the public and private sectors to challenge and deepen the discourse around the trends, technologies, and policies transforming the future of our cities

Transit Equity Day: Celebrate Public Transit and Envision the Future!
Feb 21, 12:00 PM | Kensington Corridor Trust, 3400 J Street
Join Transit Forward Philadelphia in person for a day dedicated to celebrating public transit and imagining what’s next! Dive into engaging conversation and activities as they explore ways to make PA's transit safe, sustainable and accessible for everyone.

Intercity Bus Terminal Open House
February 25, 6-8 PM | Independence Visitor Center, 599 Market St
The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is hosting an open house to gather community input on their plans for a permanent home for Philadelphia's intercity bus operations.

Urbanist Fireside Chat with Angela Brooks
February 26, 6pm to 8pm | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join our Housing Committee for a “fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

DVRPC Planning and Funding Transportation Infrastructure Across the Region
Mar 4, 06:00 PM | Virtual via Zoom
Join DVRPC for a webinar that will inform and engage residents in major regional planning and transportation initiatives. It will provide an overview of long-range planning efforts for Update: Connections 2050, explain the Transportation Improvement Program (TIP), how projects are prioritized, and show how residents can provide feedback to help shape planning decisions.

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference
Thursday, March 12th, 9:00am to 4:00pm | Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St
This year's Vision Zero conference, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety", invites participants to explore how the physical, social, and economic city converge and what’s possible when community needs and lived experiences guide decisions

WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Spotlight PA / Shapiro wants PA to be a leader on home construction
  • WHYY / West Philly apartment building will bring 40 affordable units to gentrifying section
  • WHYY / Gov. Shapiro announces $1B housing plan to spur new developments in Pennsylvania

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • WHYY / Center City transformation into more of a residential neighborhood continues

  • PhillyVoice / Philly to put up 'No Stopping' signs along bike lanes citywide after receiving $1 million from PennDOT

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #12 — February 11, 2026
item.description:
🗳️ TONIGHT: RUN FOR COMMITTEE PERSON TRAINING

Tonight at 6pm, learn how to run for committee person!

Committee persons play important and influential roles in Philadelphia politics, but the ward system can feel confusing and opaque.

Our sister-org Fifth Square PAC will be co-hosting an in-person training tonight in Center City which will provide a practical guide to Philadelphia's ward system and teach you how to run for committee person.

REGISTER HERE

 

Can't make it tonight? There's a virtual option tomorrow from 6-7pm.

❌ CITY COUNCIL SAYS NO I-95 WIDENING

This past week, City Council passed a resolution opposing PennDOT's plans to expand I-95 throughout South Philly and Center City.

Despite abundant evidence that adding new lanes increases pollution and harms surrounding communities, PennDOT is set on expanding ramps and adding new lanes, even at the cost of destroying youth sports facilities.

We strongly oppose I-95 expansion and we thank CM Squilla and City Council for standing with Philadelphians to protect our city.

Read more about the resolution from Broad and Market.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

Join our Housing Committee on February 26th for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

We will be hosting it at Indy Hall and providing hoagies, beer, and seltzers.

RSVP HERE

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #10 — January 28, 2026
item.description:
🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads.

There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024.

SIGN OUR PETITION

 

Together with Philly Bike Action, we're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer with a series of immediate and long-term changes to reduce speeding and remove unnecessary conflict areas between road users.

PBA is also looking for volunteers to help with flyer distribution and in-person petitioning.

⛔ NO PARKING FOR ICE

We strongly condemn the Philadelphia Parking Authority’s decision to contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to provide indoor parking garage space for their vehicles.

In Minneapolis and other cities, the deployment of federal immigration enforcement has led to violent confrontations, chaotic scenes, displacement of families, and even death.

We urge PPA to publicly promise not to sign additional contracts with ICE. See our full statement here.

🚇 HELP FIGHT FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

This Friday, join us and Transit for All PA at Fox Chase Regional Rail Station for a morning of canvassing transit riders followed by a press conference calling on Governor Shapiro to prioritize transit funding in the state budget.

🦺 2026 VISION ZERO CONFERENCE

Save the date for this year's Vision Zero Conference!

The 2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference will be held on March 12th on Temple's campus.

The day-long conference will feature local and nationally-recognized speakers & panelists, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety"

item.content:encoded:
🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads.

There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024.

SIGN OUR PETITION

 

Together with Philly Bike Action, we're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer with a series of immediate and long-term changes to reduce speeding and remove unnecessary conflict areas between road users.

PBA is also looking for volunteers to help with flyer distribution and in-person petitioning.

⛔ NO PARKING FOR ICE

We strongly condemn the Philadelphia Parking Authority’s decision to contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to provide indoor parking garage space for their vehicles.

In Minneapolis and other cities, the deployment of federal immigration enforcement has led to violent confrontations, chaotic scenes, displacement of families, and even death.

We urge PPA to publicly promise not to sign additional contracts with ICE. See our full statement here.

🚇 HELP FIGHT FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

This Friday, join us and Transit for All PA at Fox Chase Regional Rail Station for a morning of canvassing transit riders followed by a press conference calling on Governor Shapiro to prioritize transit funding in the state budget.

🦺 2026 VISION ZERO CONFERENCE

Save the date for this year's Vision Zero Conference!

The 2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference will be held on March 12th on Temple's campus.

The day-long conference will feature local and nationally-recognized speakers & panelists, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety"

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.
